title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents, partners and stakeholders to respect, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: The following are the major global deliverables and activities of the ILO in this policy area. (1) Ratification campaigns of all fundamental standards, especially the Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise Convention, 1948 (No. 87), the Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining Convention, 1949 (No. 98), Conventions Nos 155 and 187 and the Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930, and development of a tripartite plan of action on fundamental principles and rights at work 2024–29, based on the outcome of the Conference recurrent discussion (2024). (2) Development of global knowledge, research products and updated policy guidance to mutually reinforce interventions related to fundamental principles and rights at work; production of new global estimates on child labour 2021–25 and tools to assess deficits, including a safe and healthy working environment and a repository on SDG target 8.7, as a follow-up of the Durban Call to Action on the Elimination of Child Labour. (3) Consolidation of partnerships, generation of innovation and capacity building through Alliance 8.7, RIILAC, EPIC, the fundamental principles and rights at work academy, ITC, Turin), regional initiatives and business networks (CLP & GBNFL). (4) Enhanced support for the annual review of the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (1998), as amended in 2022, prioritizing technical assistance requested by Member States in their annual reports.
